title: Pro-étale trace and its integral image on a splitting
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology and valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ with the subspace topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For each scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], use its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], continuous coefficient ring sheaves $A_T(U)=C(|U|,A)$ and $E_T(U)=C(|U|,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], and sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $p:V\to S$ be a finite étale scheme morphism [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], let $L$ be an $E_S$-module, and let $M\subseteq p^*L$ be an $A_V$-submodule. Here inverse image is canonical coefficient pullback [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and $p_*$ is direct image of sheaves, evaluated by $p_*F(U)=F(V\times_SU)$. There is a unique $E_S$-linear map $\operatorname{Tr}:p_*p^*L\to L$ whose restriction to every étale splitting $V\times_SU\cong\coprod_{j\in J}U$ is $(s_j)\mapsto\sum_js_j$. Define $N\subseteq L$ as the sheaf image of $p_*M\to p_*p^*L\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tr}}L$, that is, sections locally represented by traces of sections of $p_*M$. Then $N$ is an $A_S$-submodule, and on every such splitting $N|_U=\sum_{j\in J}M_j$ as submodule sheaves of $L|_U$, where $M_j$ is the restriction of $M$ to the $j$-th sheet.

proof.text: Work in the compatible small sites and larger universe of the statement. For any site object $r:W\to S$, the weakly étale localization lemma identifies $W_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with $S_{\mathrm{proét}}/W$. Clause (1) of the object inverse-image restriction lemma identifies $r^{-1}G$ with $G|_W$ for arbitrary abelian and ring sheaves, not only constant coefficients. In particular $r^{-1}T_S$ identifies with $T_S|_W=T_W$ for $T=A,E$: both evaluate on $Z\to W$ as $C(|Z|,T)$. The canonical map $c_r:r^{-1}T_S\to T_W$ is the adjunct of precomposition along $W\times_SZ\to Z$; under the restriction identification its component is identity, because the distinguished map $Z\to W\times_SZ$ followed by that projection is $\mathrm{id}_Z$. Thus canonical module pullback along $r$ is restriction: the scalar-extension isomorphism sends $t\otimes m$ to $tm$, with inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. These maps commute with restriction and are inverse already on the presheaf tensors, hence on their sheafifications. The same identifications apply to arrows between site objects by relocalization.

source.place: Tags 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products), 00Y0 (definition-localize), 03EH (lemma-relocalize); proetale.tex Tag 09A5; continuous coefficient specialization written out here

proof.text: Apply the finite étale local-splitting lemma to $p$ at each point of $S$. Obtain a jointly surjective étale family $\{U_a\to S\}$ and finite sets $J_a$ with $V\times_SU_a\cong\coprod_{j\in J_a}U_a$. This is a covering in the small pro-étale site by the étale/pro-étale covering lemma. Its members and $V$ are weakly étale over $S$ by clause (1) of the étale comparison lemma, so step 1 applies to them. No constant degree or surjectivity of $p$ is assumed: the sets $J_a$ can vary and can be empty.

Fix any splitting over an étale $U\to S$ and any $Z\to U$ in $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Its pullback is the disjoint union of $J$ copies of $Z$. By step 1, $(p^*L)$ restricted to each sheet is $L|_U$. Its finitely many sheets are open immersions, hence étale and jointly surjective, so they form a pro-étale covering by the étale/pro-étale covering lemma; the sheaf equalizer axiom on this disjoint open cover gives $(p_*p^*L)|_U(Z)=\prod_{j\in J}L|_U(Z)$ and $(p_*M)|_U(Z)=\prod_{j\in J}M_j(Z)$: mixed intersections are empty, a sheaf of modules has its zero group on the empty object by the empty-cover axiom, so every tuple is matching and glues uniquely. Define $\tau_{U,Z}((s_j))=\sum_{j\in J}s_j$. The coefficient action is diagonal, since a function $Z\to E$ pulls back to the same function on every sheet. Distributivity gives $\tau_{U,Z}(a(s_j))=a\tau_{U,Z}((s_j))$, and restrictions commute with the sum. Hence these are $E_U$-linear sheaf maps. For $J=\varnothing$ the domain is zero and the map is zero.

source.place: Pushing down by the trace: splitting into copies and the trace is their sum; sheaf equalizer calculation written out

proof.text: The maps of step 3 agree on overlaps without a connectedness assumption. Indeed over $W=U\times_SU'$ two splittings identify the same scheme with $\coprod_JW$ and $\coprod_KW$. Intersect its $j$-th component in the first decomposition with its $k$-th component in the second. Viewed inside the first component $W$, these intersections are open and closed subsets $C_{jk}$; for each $j$ they partition $W$, and at each point they give a bijection between the two finite sets of sheets. For every bijection $\sigma:J\to K$, the open and closed subset $\bigcap_j C_{j,\sigma(j)}$ is therefore a locus where the decompositions differ by that fixed permutation; these finitely many subsets cover $W$, and pulled back to any $Z\to W$ they form a pro-étale covering by the étale/pro-étale covering lemma. If there is no bijection, $W$ is empty. On each subset the two maps are equal by reindexing the finite sum, and equality on $W$ follows from the sheaf separatedness axiom. The identical argument compares the chosen cover with any other splitting.

source.place: Pushing down by the trace: independence of the local splitting, expanded by intersections of sheet components

proof.text: Apply the map-gluing clause of sheaf covering descent to the underlying sheaves of sets $P=p_*p^*L$, $Q=L$ and the covering of step 2. Its hypotheses hold: the small pro-étale site is small in the chosen larger universe, has fibre products (base change and composition preserve weakly étale maps), the family covers, and its double-overlap maps agree by step 4. Obtain a unique sheaf map $\operatorname{Tr}:P\to L$ restricting to the chosen sums. It is additive and $E_S$-linear because those equalities can be checked after restricting a section to that cover, where step 3 proves them, and then using separatedness of $L$. Comparing with any splitting on its pullback of the chosen cover, step 4 and separatedness give its required sum formula. Any other map with all the sum formulas agrees on the chosen cover and therefore equals $\operatorname{Tr}$.

source.place: Tag 04TQ (lemma-glue-maps), applied to the small pro-étale site; blueprint trace paragraph

proof.text: Let $q:p_*M\to L$ be inclusion followed by the trace, using the inclusion $A_S\to E_S$ on scalars. It is $A_S$-linear: a section of $A_S$ acts on $M$ by its pullback to $V$, and the inclusion and the trace preserve this action. Define $N(Z)$ to be those $s\in L(Z)$ which on a covering $\{Z_b\to Z\}$ are $q(m_b)$ for $m_b\in(p_*M)(Z_b)$, exactly the sheaf image specified in the statement. Pullbacks of witnessing covers show stability under restriction. Zero is represented by zero; on a common refinement of two witnessing covers, $q(m)+q(m')=q(m+m')$, $-q(m)=q(-m)$, and $a q(m)=q((a|_{Z_b})m)$. Thus $N(Z)$ is an $A_S(Z)$-submodule. If matching sections of $N$ are glued in $L$, compose their covers of local lifts with the original cover: transitivity of covers supplies local lifts of the glued section. Hence $N$ is a subsheaf and an $A_S$-submodule of $L$, without assuming that $q$ is surjective on global sections.

source.place: Pushing down by the trace: image of the composite; local-image and module-closure argument

proof.text: Restrict to any splitting over $U$. The witnessing-cover definition of $N$ is unchanged on the slice: covers there are precisely covers of the underlying objects. By step 3 the map $q$ on this slice is $\prod_jM_j\to L|_U$, $(m_j)\mapsto\sum_jm_j$. Let $\sum_jM_j$ mean the smallest submodule sheaf of $L|_U$ containing each $M_j$; equivalently its sections locally are finite sums with one term in each $M_j$. This description is a subsheaf by the same cover-composition argument as step 6; it contains each $M_j$ by using zero in the other coordinates, and every submodule sheaf containing the $M_j$ contains these local sums by gluing. Every local trace is such a sum, giving $N|_U\subseteq\sum_jM_j$. Conversely a locally represented sum is the trace of its tuple, which is a section of $p_*M$ by the disjoint-cover gluing of step 3, giving the reverse inclusion. If individual summands are initially specified on different covers, their finitely many covers admit a common refinement by successive pullbacks. For $J=\varnothing$ both sides are zero. This proves the asserted equality of submodule sheaves.

split_report.summary: Construct the trace from finite étale local splittings, verify locally varying permutation invariance, glue the linear maps, and compute the integral sheaf image by local representatives. Reuse existing generic tools; no new nodes. All coefficients are continuous ring sheaves, not constant sheaves. Empty fibres, variable degree, arbitrary modules and sheaf rather than sectionwise images are covered.
split_report.blueprint: sk-lem-stratified-lattice proof, Pushing down by the trace: the definition of Tr and the image composite, and the sentence that on a splitting the trace is the sum and L_0=M_1+...+M_d. No lattice-freeness or lisseness claims are used.

tool_uses.why: Generic identification of the pro-étale slice site for a site object, used to interpret restrictions; it does not replace the trace argument.
Specifies the canonical continuous coefficient map as the adjunct of projection precomposition; its restriction is explicitly calculated as identity in step 1.
Only the generic map-gluing clause for sheaves of sets is used; all trace maps, overlap agreement, and linearity are established in this item.
Only étale implies weakly étale, allowing finite étale arrows as pro-étale site objects, is used.
Generic stability of weakly étale maps supplies fibre products in the presenting site, a hypothesis of the map-gluing lemma.
